deep.reconstruction:
Observing-journal page from a latitude (Polhöhe) campaign, probably Göttingen c. 1812–1814. The method is repeated circum-meridian zenith distances of circumpolar stars at lower culmination, taken with a repeating (multiplying) circle. Two clocks appear: 'Shelton' and 'Uhr' (the Kampe clock).

(A) 17 March, a Cephei star.
- Six pointings were timed between 9h20'03" and 9h44'53". The circle read 234°46'15.25" after 4 pointings and 352°08'54.50" after 6.
- Mean single zenith distances: 4-fold, 234°46'15.25"/4 = 58°41'33.81"; 6-fold, 352°08'54.50"/6 = 58°41'29.08".
- Reduction to the meridian is added, because the star is at lower culmination. The individual reductions are not written. The summed corrections are 33.73" (4-fold) and 40.22" (6-fold), giving 58°42'07.54" and 58°42'09.30".
- Refraction is computed in logarithms: log(barometer factor, 27 in 8 lines) 9.9935 + log(thermometer factor, +0.75 °R) 0.0152 + log(mean refraction at z≈58°42') 1.9805 = 1.9892 (mod 10). Hence R = 10^1.9892 = 97.54" = 1'37.54".
- Corrected zenith distances: 58°43'45.08" (4-fold) and 58°43'46.84" (6-fold).
- At lower culmination z = 180° − φ − δ, so φ = 180° − z − δ. Using the 6-fold value and δ = 69°44'18.39": φ = 180° − 58°43'46.84" − 69°44'18.39" = 51°31'54.77".
- Two caveats. The star name is uncertain ('γ'/'ε' Cephei), and the adopted 69°44' is not a modern γ or ε Cephei declination; I have not identified it. With the 4-fold value one gets 51°31'56.53", which is not written.

(B) 20 March, α Ursae Minoris (Polaris) at lower culmination.
- Clock time of culmination = RA 0h54'48.82" + Shelton correction 6'50.37" − Kampe–Shelton difference 0'38" = 1h01'01.19". This is read as 13h01'01" on the clock.
- The clock comparisons at the foot of the page (Uhr − Shelton = −37.5" at 12h47', −38.4" at 13h31') justify the −38".
- There are ten pointings at 12h53'20" … 13h19'11". The hour angles t from 13h01'01" are: 7'41", 5'08", 0'40", 1'52", 5'08", 7'54", 10'12", 12'39", 15'52", 18'10" (time). All are correct.
- Reductions to the meridian (my reconstruction of the formula used): Δz = A·2 sin²(t/2)/sin1", with A = cosφ cosδ / sin z ≈ 0.6220·0.02947/0.6449 ≈ 0.0284.
- Listed reductions: 3.29, 1.47, 0.02, 0.20 (looks like 0.26), 1.47, 3.48, 5.81, 8.93, 14.04, 18.41. Sum 57.12".
- Circle reading after 10 pointings: 401°24'59.25" + 57.12" = 401°25'56.37". Dividing by 10 gives 40°08'35.64".
- Refraction +49.84" (barometer 27 in 8.9 lines, thermometer +2.5 °R) gives z = 40°09'25.48".
- With δ(Polaris) = 88°18'40.13": φ = 180° − 88°18'40.13" − 40°09'25.48" = 51°31'54.39". This is labelled 'Polhöhe aus 10 B.' (latitude from 10 observations).
- The adjacent pages give 51°31'56.16" (15 March, Cephei star) and 51°31'55.09" (22 March, Polaris, 18 obs.). The next page combines 10 and 18 observations to 28: 51°31'54.39" and 55.09" → 54.84".
errors: Fourth Polaris reduction (t = 1'52"): the correct value is A·t²/2 ≈ 0.19". The written figure looks like 0.26. However, the column total 57.12" equals the sum only if this entry is 0.20 (with 0.26 the sum is 57.18"). So either the entry reads 0.20 or the total silently uses ~0.20; either way the final result is unaffected.

All other divisions, additions, hour angles, logarithmic refraction sums and the final latitudes check to within 0.01". The 17 March latitude 51°31'54.77" uses the 6-fold mean; the 4-fold mean would give 51°31'56.53", which is not stated.

results.what: Latitude from repeated zenith distances of circumpolar stars at lower culmination, φ = 180° − z − δ, using a Borda/Reichenbach repeating circle
results.modern_name: Latitude determination by circum-meridian altitudes (lower culmination)

results.what: Reduction to the meridian Δz = (cosφ cosδ / sin z)·2 sin²(t/2)/sin1"
Logarithmic refraction computation: log mean refraction + barometric and thermometric log factors

deep.surprise_reason: Routine observatory reduction of latitude observations with a repeating circle, typical of Gauss's Göttingen practice. No new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: phi = 180° − z − δ gives 51°31'54.77" on 17 March (result 0)
sum of reductions = 57.12 with fourth entry 0.20

transcription_corrections: The Polaris reduction for t=1'52" should probably read 0.20 (transcribed 0.26); the total 57.12 requires 0.20.
'Kampez' is 'Kampe z.' (Kampe clock compared with Shelton), consistent with 'Shelton Kampe' on the next page.
Star name on 17 March is uncertain ('γ' vs 'ε' Cepheus); the previous page has ε Cephei with the same δ value 69°44'18".
